reasoning_summary: Steps 0001-0025 are fine: Lemma 1 (sup in L2 of any T subseteq S3 lies in S3), Lemma 2 (inf in L2 of any finite F subseteq S3 lies in S3), and the recalled definition at 0025 that a frame homomorphism is exactly a finite-meet-preserving, arbitrary-join-preserving map. The join-preservation section then breaks down. Line 0029 already mis-states the hypothesis: to show phi restricted to S1 x S3 preserves arbitrary joins one must take A subseteq S1 (the domain), not A subseteq S3 subseteq S2; with A subseteq S3 the expression bigvee_1 A at line 0033-0034 is not even defined, and phi[A] is meaningless. The decisive failure is line 0037, which asserts phi(bigvee_1 A) = bigwedge_2 phi[A] 'by definition of Frame Homomorphism'. The definition just recalled at line 0025 (and the gloss at line 0048, which explicitly says the displayed symbols denote suprema in L1, L2, L3) gives phi(bigvee_1 A) = bigvee_2 phi[A]; a frame homomorphism does not send an arbitrary join to a meet, so the cited justification supports the opposite of what is written and the display contradicts the proof's own gloss at 0048. The error propagates: line 0040 converts bigwedge_2 phi[A] to bigwedge_3 phi[A] citing Lemma 1, which is a statement about suprema, not infima; the only lemma about infima (Lemma 2) requires F finite, whereas A here is arbitrary, so no available lemma justifies that transfer either. Consequently the chain 0033-0046 never establishes phi(bigvee_1 A) = bigvee_3 phi[A], and the conclusion at line 0050 that the restriction is arbitrary join preserving is unsupported. (The parallel meet section 0055-0076 is structurally correct apart from the same domain slip 'F subseteq S3' instead of F subseteq S1.) Stopping at 0037 per the early-stop protocol.
